content.text:
This confirms the bug: `lookupValue` calls `value.equalsIgnoreCase(...)`, so when `value` is `null` (query has a single-choice parameter like SUBJECT/DEPARTMENT but no matching request parameter was actually supplied), it throws a `NullPointerException`, breaking CSV export. The fix adds a `null` check before processing.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 0dd84a04f05c4a852194e92db650588d1a8166c0

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the file history of `SavedHqlExportToCSV.java` with `git log --follow` and `git log -p --follow` to find when the exact code block modified by the fix (`String value = helper.getParameter(option.name()); ... option.lookupValue(...) ... params.add(v);`) was introduced.

**(2) Specific change:** Commit `0dd84a04f` ("HQL Reports: Export HQL") introduced the single-choice parameter handling branch:
```java
String value = helper.getParameter(option.name());
SavedHQLInterface.IdValue v = new SavedHQLInterface.IdValue();
v.setValue(option.name());
Long id = option.lookupValue(context.getUser(), value);
...
```
This code unconditionally calls `option.lookupValue(context.getUser(), value)` even when `helper.getParameter(option.name())` returns `null` (i.e., no value was supplied for that single-choice option in the request). The fix commit `395d7ef9f` wraps this whole block in `if (value != null) { ... }` to skip processing when no value is present.

**(3) Supporting evidence:** I inspected `SavedHQL.java`'s `lookupValue` implementations (e.g., for `DEPARTMENT`, `SUBJECT`, `SESSION` options), which all call `value.equalsIgnoreCase(...)` or `.setString("term", value)` directly on the `value` parameter without a null check. When `value` is `null`, `value.equalsIgnoreCase(...)` throws a `NullPointerException`, causing CSV export to fail — exactly matching the bug description ("fixed ability to export HQL report as CSV when the query contains a single-choice parameter"). This code path (added in `0dd84a04f`) remained essentially unchanged (only refactored, not logic-fixed) through subsequent commits `e0793ff4c` and up to the buggy state fixed by `395d7ef9f`.

Confidence: high. The introduced code and the null-unsafe `lookupValue` implementations directly explain the reported bug, and the fix commit's change (adding a null guard) precisely negates the defect introduced in `0dd84a04f`.
